_comment: ENUM-PARITY BASELINE. Read by tests/enum-parity.test.ts. One number per service: the maximum
count of DISTINCT Zod enum sites that no PHP enum resolves to, by rule key, manual bridge or
class name. IT MAY ONLY SHRINK. The gate prints the new number the moment it falls, and fails
when it rises, exactly like ratchet.json and the allow-lists next to it. Never raise it to turn
a red suite green: an unmapped enum is a value list we promise an agent and compare to nothing.
Distinct SITES, not occurrences: one shared value object reached from 99 tools is one unpinned
promise and one edit, and counting it 99 times would make the number a popularity contest.
What is in the count today, by class (run pnpm test to print the full list with an owning tool):
1. sort.field / sort.direction / include.* / group_by on searches whose FormRequest constrains
none of them: 29 of the 34 sites left on 2026-08-16 (linkedin 21, id 4, orchestration 4).
gtm.service.id resolves nearly all of these positionally because its search requests carry
Rule::in; most linkedin and orchestration ones declare 'nullable' only, so our Zod enum is
STRICTER than the backend rather than drifting from it. Clears one FormRequest at a time,
backend side.
2. Five singles with no PHP enum behind them at all: the latest-engine refresh stop_reason, the
analytics change_direction, the recommendations direction and the job-search workplace_type
(all linkedin), plus the webhook test-send error_kind (orchestration). The notifications
group_by that used to sit in this class is resolved by Rule::in now.
2026-08-16: the CreditsSpentValue.reason / .executed_on class left this count with the
platform-wide credits removal. The value object is deleted, so no Zod site reaches it and no
promotion of its class constants to a real enum is owed any more. Ceilings re-derived from that
same run: linkedin 27 -> 25, id 7 -> 4, orchestration 7 -> 5.
